v.1.1.0 2026-09-21 01:27 UTC PSVitaAlive: 1.1.0
PSVitaAlive 1.1.0

The Impossible Game — PS Vita Port v1.1.0

Adds full support for the official Level Pack add-on (3 extra levels), on top of the playable base port from v1.0.0. Runs libimpossible.so directly on ARM via a soloader + FalsoJNI, with OpenGL ES 1.1 (fixed-function pipeline) rendering through vitaGL.

✨ What's New

  • 5 levels playable: the 2 base levels (Fire Aura, Original Xbox Level) plus the 3 levels from the official Level Pack (Chaoz Fantasy, Heaven, Phazd) — confirmed working on real hardware with audio, input, and save data.
  • Level Pack .so support: the loader now resolves the Level Pack's libimpossible.so (same 11 JNI exports, impossiblegamelevelpack symbol prefix instead of impossiblegame) — no source changes needed to swap between the base and Level Pack .so.
  • Save data expanded: 6 → 12 medals, 2 → 5 levels of practice/no-flag progress tracking.
  • Menu scaled to 5 levels: level select grew from 2 to 5 buttons (3+2 grid with a back button), Stats and Medals screens grew from 3 to 6 subpages each.
  • Per-level music: added BGM_SOUNDTRACK2/3/4 for Chaoz Fantasy/Heaven/Phazd; the 2 base levels keep using the original soundtrack.ogg.

⚠️ Known Issues / Pending Work

  • None currently open. The Level Pack's statspage4/5/6.png assets only ship at their original mdpi resolution (no landscape crop like the base game's stats pages) — a minor, cosmetic sharpness difference only, not a functional issue.
  • Updating an existing install resets save.dat (the save layout grew to fit 5 levels / 12 medals) — expected, not a bug.

📋 Requirements

  • PS Vita / PS TV running Custom Firmware (HENkaku or Enso), firmware 3.60/3.65+.
  • kubridge installed as a kernel plugin.
  • libshacccg.suprx installed in ur0:data/.
  • A legally obtained copy of The Impossible Game for Android (05133-the-impossible-1.5.2.apk, package com.flukedude.impossiblegame).
  • (Optional, for the 3 extra levels) A legally obtained copy of the Level Pack add-on (05133-Impossible-Level-Pack.apk, package com.flukedude.impossiblegamelevelpack).

📦 Installation

  1. Install theimpossiblegame.vpk with VitaShell.
  2. Copy the contents of ux0_data/theimpossiblegame/ to ux0:data/theimpossiblegame/ on the console (see README.md for the full file layout).
  3. For the 3 extra levels: unzip 05133-Impossible-Level-Pack.apk on your PC and merge its .so, soundtrack2/3/4.ogg, and level-select/stats/medals PNGs into ux0:data/theimpossiblegame/ — see the Level Pack Installation section in README.md for the exact file list and paths. Without this step, the game still runs fine with just the 2 base levels.

See README.md for the full port description, and port_progress.md for the bug-by-bug diagnosis log (every fix confirmed on real hardware, no guessing).

Smash Melee Vita

Smash Melee Vita 0.7.1 (experimental build 25.1)
↻ Pendiente PSVitaAlivePRE-RELEASE
vita-v0.7.1-build.25.1 2026-09-20 09:10 UTC PSVitaAlive: 0.7.1
PSVitaAlive 0.7.1 → release vita-v0.7.1-build.25.1

Experimental PS Vita build for testing. Back up your saves before updating.

What's new in build 25.1

  • Added a hidden DEBUG TOOLS option that opens Melee's original developer menus. It includes match setup, item and Pokemon spawning, debug cameras, collision displays, sound tests, and other internal tools.
  • Normal play is unchanged. Debug Tools stays hidden until deliberately unlocked, remains available only for the current app session, and disappears after the game is closed.
  • Dangerous save, memory-card, global-state, and unsupported hardware actions are disabled.
  • Fixed the Debug Tools label so it reappears after leaving the developer menu, returning through the title screen, and reopening Options.
  • Expanded the built-in shader cache to 1,785 shaders, including 209 additional programs contributed from another Vita. This should reduce more first-time shader stutters, although uncommon effects may still stutter once.

Hidden Debug Tools

This build includes Melee's original developer menus for testing matches, items, cameras, collision displays, sound, and other internal features. Nothing appears during normal play. To reveal DEBUG TOOLS, open Options and enter Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, Select on the D-pad. The unlock lasts only until the application closes.

These menus were designed for developers, so some combinations may behave strangely. Dangerous save, memory-card, and unsupported hardware actions are disabled. Read the attached DEBUG-TOOLS.md before using them; it explains the Vita controls, safe functions, camera, item spawner, and how to leave a debug match.

Opening Debug Tools

  1. Open Options from Melee's main menu.
  2. Enter Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, Select using the digital D-pad.
  3. Select the newly revealed DEBUG TOOLS row.

The unlock is not saved and must be entered again after closing the game.

Vita Cross acts as GameCube A, Circle acts as B, Square acts as X, Triangle acts as Y, and Select acts as Z. In a debug match, hold Square and tap D-pad Up to open the normal pause menu, then use its exit option. Tap D-pad Up by itself to cycle the debug camera.

Read the attached DEBUG-TOOLS.md for the complete controls, item spawner, camera modes, visualization tools, safety limitations, and recovery steps.

Other 0.7.1 improvements

  • Corrected lighting for Trophy Gallery trophies and gameplay objects.
  • Restored Snag the Trophies fog and fixed copied-screen effects.
  • Fixed boxed item effects, Stage Clear flicker, and missing stage elements.
  • Fixed the first-Goomba Adventure Mode crash and a copied-screen transition crash seen near the end of Adventure Mode.
  • Vita R acts as the GameCube R trigger, and Select acts as Z.
  • Updated the LiveArea icon and backgrounds.

Install notes

  • Install SmashMeleevita.vpk with VitaShell.
  • Keep ux0:data/melee/shadercache/ when updating; the game continues learning shaders that are not built in.
  • Requires your own uncompressed USA revision 2 / NTSC-U 1.02 GALE01.iso and ur0:data/libshacccg.suprx. Neither is included.
  • Title ID remains MLVITA002; package version is 00.71.
  • This is an optimized Release build. Logging and debugger support are disabled.

Asphalt 5

Asphalt 5 HD - PS Vita Port v1.0.3
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlive
v1.0.3 2026-09-20 04:47 UTC PSVitaAlive: 1.0.3
PSVitaAlive 1.0.3

Asphalt 5 HD - PS Vita Port v1.0.3

We are incredibly excited to announce the first public Beta release of Asphalt 5 for the PS Vita!

This port uses a custom Android wrapper (soLoader/FalsoJNI) to run the original ARMv6 Android executable natively on the Vita, fully hardware-accelerated via vitaGL.

Since this is a Beta release, the game is fully playable from start to finish, but please keep in mind that there are still some minor bugs and details being ironed out.

✨ Key Features in this Beta:

  • Full Physical Controls Integration: We've built a custom input router that seamlessly bridges Vita physical buttons with the game's native touch engine. It only works with the Touch Buttons control scheme (not Tilt or the drag-to-steer variants) — this is now forced automatically the very first time you run the port, before any save file exists.
    • Menus: Fully navigable using the D-Pad or Left Analog Stick (Up/Down). Use ❌ (Cross) to select and ⭕ (Circle) to go back.
    • Title Screens: Press any face button to instantly skip splash screens.
    • In-Game Racing:
      • D-Pad Left/Right, L/R Triggers, or Left Analog Stick to Steer.
      • ❌ (Cross) to trigger Nitrous.
      • 🟥 (Square) to Brake / Drift.
      • Start to Pause (Circle no longer duplicates this in-race — it's menu-only Back now).
  • Custom Optimized Audio Engine: The original Android game used heavy floating-point math for audio mixing, which crippled the Vita's CPU. We wrote a custom 32-bit fixed-point audio mixer from scratch with Linear Interpolation, providing perfectly smooth engine pitches, zero stuttering, and high-fidelity 48kHz audio output through the Vita's MAIN audio port. It follows the engine's own routing: looped sounds (engine hum, skids) track RPM live, long music tracks get a dedicated voice that SFX can never steal, and the master bus uses a soft limiter so heavy scenes don't square-wave.
  • Hardware Accelerated Graphics: Running buttery smooth thanks to vitaGL.
  • Post-Race Flow: Results screens advance with a tap anywhere, or with ❌ (Cross) on the pad — held steering/nitro from the race is cleanly released at the state change, so no more stuck input after crossing the finish line.
  • Intro & Cutscene Video Playback: The game's original MPEG-4 .mp4 cutscenes (which the Vita has no hardware decoder for) play in software at a smooth 30 FPS with in-sync audio — the intro trailer (A5_Ultimate_VNFS_2.mp4) and the in-race videos alike. Videos are decoded at half resolution and upscaled, so motion stays fluid; press ❌ (Cross) or Start at any time to skip.
  • No Screen-Off Freeze: The port resets the Vita's idle timer every frame, so the console's auto power-save can no longer turn the screen off and freeze the game while you read a menu.

⚠️ Known Issues / Beta Status:

  • Open issue — Touch Buttons icons still visible, and Nitro often needs several presses: the on-screen brake/nitro icons are drawn even though physical controls work, and ❌ (Cross) frequently needs multiple presses before Nitro actually fires — except pressing 🟥 (Square, brake/drift) immediately before ❌ (Cross), which reliably triggers Nitro on the very first try. Root cause not isolated yet; we need a console log capturing that exact drift-then-nitro pattern to fix it for real instead of guessing.
  • Recent adjustments (build clean, not yet confirmed on real hardware): left analog stick steering, a sharper internal render resolution (800x480 instead of 720x432), Touch Buttons forced as the default control scheme on first run, and Circle no longer opening the pause menu mid-race (Start already did that, so the overlap was removed).
  • This is a Beta! You might encounter occasional UI quirks or unmapped buttons in very specific sub-menus.
  • Performance is mostly solid, but some heavy tracks might experience slight frame drops. Further optimizations are planned.
  • The intro trailer needs its .mp4 present in ux0:data/asphalt5/data/ — otherwise it is skipped.
  • Manual standby with the power button (sleep/resume) is still untested — leaving the game idle is safe, but putting the console to sleep mid-game may not resume cleanly yet.

🛠️ Installation Instructions:

  1. Install libshacccg.suprx if you don't have it already (required for vitaGL).
  2. Install the provided Asphalt5.vpk.
  3. Extract the game data files (assets) into ux0:data/asphalt5/. (Note: Data files are not provided with this release; you must extract them from your own legally obtained copy of the Android game).
  4. Launch the game and enjoy!

A huge thanks to the PS Vita homebrew community and the vitaGL contributors for making this possible! Let us know your feedback and bug reports.

Shadow Guardian

Shadow Guardian Vita v1.3
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlive
v1.3 2026-09-20 04:30 UTC PSVitaAlive: 1.3.0
PSVitaAlive 1.3.0

Shadow Guardian Vita v1.3

This is a wrapper/port of Shadow Guardian HD for the PS Vita.

Changelog

  • v1.3: Full controls rework based on hardware testing feedback:
    • Wrong weapon-switch position fixed. The old touch coordinate for the weapon icon was only measured by eye and turned out to sit inside the FIRE button's touch hit-radius, so pressing that button fired the gun instead of switching weapons. All button positions (fire, aim, contextual action, grab, weapon) were re-measured with a pixel grid over a real 960x544 gameplay screenshot.
    • Weapon switch moved to Square and reworked as a swipe, not a tap. Reading the engine's own input handler (out_ghidra.c:86760-86813) showed the real weapon selector responds to the drag delta of a touch (Actor::SetNextWeapon() / SetPreviousWeapon() picked by the sign of the movement, matching its actual "left/right arrow slider" look), not a fixed tap zone — so Square now sends a synthetic down → drag-right → release over the weapon icon instead of a plain tap.
    • Circle reassigned from a debug visibility toggle to Grab/interact (the hand icon never had a physical button before); Select now toggles the touch controls on/off, taking over the old debug-toggle role.
    • Square no longer shares the Aim spot with L — only L aims now.
    • Virtual button hiding is now enforced every frame instead of once at startup, fixing buttons (the aim reticle in particular) that the engine would silently re-show later in a session.
    • Hooked GS_GamePlay::HighlightButton so the button-highlight glow shown during aim feedback / "touch this button" tutorial prompts is suppressed while the touch controls are hidden, instead of glowing over an otherwise-invisible button.
    • The weapon-selector graphics are hidden too now (previously always shown by request), using the exact GUI item index range (0xb-0x20) the engine itself uses to fade them out.
    • Free-look camera (right stick) rewritten from an absolute stick-to-touch-position mapping — which hard-capped at a fixed offset and could never complete a full turn — to a continuous relative drag with invisible wraparound recentring, so holding the stick now keeps rotating indefinitely: slow and precise at a light tilt, fast at full tilt, a full 360° around the character is now possible.
    • Fixed a blurry intro video. A texture-downsampling optimization was quartering the effective resolution of logo.m4v before a 4x upscale to the screen; disabled, since the intro is only a few seconds and the blur wasn't worth the saved upload bandwidth.

Setup Instructions

In order to properly install the game, you'll need to extract the data from the original Android game.

  1. Install the kubridge and fd_fix plugins on your PS Vita.
  2. Install libshacccg.suprx, if you don't have it already, by following this guide.
  3. Obtain the original APK of Shadow Guardian (Shadow-Guardian-HD-v1-0-1-UK-RU.apk) and the required data files.
  4. Extract the .apk using any zip extractor.
  5. Place the executable libshadowguardian.so (from lib/armeabi-v7a/ inside the APK) in ux0:data/shadowguardian/. (If the APK also contains libStormGLOFT.so, you can copy it too — it does no harm.)
  6. Place all game asset folders (res, shaders, textures, models, music, sounds, etc.) in ux0:data/shadowguardian/.
  7. Make sure the 16:9 assets sprites_1_7 and gui_1_7 are present. If the APK only ships the sprites_1_6 / gui_1_6 variants, duplicate them with VitaShell (Copy + Paste + Rename) so the _1_7 names exist — missing 16:9 GUI assets can crash the game on the LOADING screen. Also confirm the res/ folder was copied.
  8. Double-check that gui_1_6 and sprites_1_6 themselves are also present in ux0:data/shadowguardian/ (not just the _1_7 copies) — some assets are only ever requested by their _1_6 name at runtime, and a copy missing just these two files can pass every other check and still crash later during gameplay.
  9. Download and install shadowguardian.vpk on your PS Vita.

Controls

  • Left Analog - Movement (in-game only)
  • Right Analog - Camera (free-look, continuous drag - hold to keep turning; light tilt for slow/precise aim, full tilt for a fast full 360°)
  • D-Pad - Menu Navigation / Movement
  • R - Fire
  • L - Aim (hold)
  • Cross - Contextual action (jump / run / climb)
  • Circle - Grab / interact
  • Square - Switch weapon
  • Start - Pause / Back
  • Select - Toggle Virtual Buttons (Hide/Show touch controls)
  • Touch Screen - Original Touch Controls

Known Issues

  • A blue highlight/glow effect shown specifically when switching weapons may still appear even with the touch controls hidden — the generic HighlightButton hook (v1.3) covers the button-prompt glow, but the weapon-change flash may come from a separate, not-yet-located effect. Please report it with a log/screenshot of the exact moment it happens.
  • Square's weapon-switch swipe and the new continuous camera drag (v1.3) are newly implemented and pending confirmation on hardware across multiple weapons/play sessions.

Troubleshooting

Crash on the LOADING screen (C2-12828-1 error): this is usually a data setup problem, not a game bug. Check the following with VitaShell:

  1. You installed the latest shadowguardian.vpk (older builds have known crashes that are already fixed).
  2. kubridge and fd_fix plugins plus libshacccg.suprx are installed (see Setup above).
  3. In ux0:data/shadowguardian/: libshadowguardian.so, the res/ folder, and all asset folders are present, and both the _1_6 and _1_7 variants of sprites and gui exist (sprites_1_6, sprites_1_7, gui_1_6, gui_1_7) — copy whichever ones are missing from the variant you do have. As of v1.2.3, a missing gui_1_6/gui_1_7 or sprites_1_6/sprites_1_7 shows a clear "missing game data files" dialog on boot instead of crashing later — if you see that dialog, it's telling you exactly which one to fix.

If it still crashes, please report it with:

  1. The newest ux0:data/shadowguardian/logs/game_log_*.txt (from the time of the crash — do not delete it).
  2. The newest ux0:data/psp2core-*-eboot.bin.psp2dmp core dump.
  3. A note on exactly when it happens (on boot, which level loading, do you ever reach the menu?).

Credits

  • TheFloW for the so_loader wrapper and Android porting boilerplate.
  • Rinnegatamante for vitaGL and porting tools.
  • Gameloft for the original game.

Deltarune Vita

Deltarune Vita v0.75 (Internal Development Build)
↻ Pendiente PSVitaAlivePRE-RELEASE
v0.75 2026-09-18 09:30 UTC PSVitaAlive: v.0.69
PSVitaAlive v.0.69 → release v0.75

[!WARNING] This is an internal development pre-release, not a release candidate. Bugs, GPU crashes, missing graphics and performance issues may still occur.

Highlights

Borders (NXRUNE mod adaptation)

Adaptation of the changes applied to the .win files of Chapters 3, 4, and 5 by the NXRUNE mod (Deltarune Borders Mod and More). The logic was adapted for the DeltaruneVita project, including the preservation of externalized border images.

Now, the borders change during specific in-game events, rather than just upon switching the current Room (as was the initial behavior of dynamic borders).

Modern-GL and shaders: GPU stability work

  • Resource collection now closes the active GXM scene and waits for submitted work before freeing retired allocations. It no longer opens a new scene immediately before collection.
  • Custom shader uniforms now use GXM-managed reservations instead of a 2 MiB circular buffer that could overwrite data still needed by earlier draws.
  • Failed uniform reservations reject the affected draw instead of copying through an invalid pointer or submitting it to the GPU. These checks remain active in release builds.
  • These changes apply to the shared renderer across rooms, including the Chapter 3 minigame and Chapter 5 Castle Town shop. Shaders remain enabled; rooms are not excluded as a workaround.

[!NOTE] Modern-GL remains experimental. The new regressions passed locally, but desktop tests do not emulate the Vita GPU. The reported hardware crashes still require confirmation with v0.75-7 on the device.

Chapter 3

  • Blue Stars border switching follows the original border_switch event rather than an audience-object heuristic, avoiding an early transition and dependence on dialogue language.
  • Synchronized texture eviction for gameshow/board rooms, plus working-set trimming and texture prewarming for room_board_2.
  • Intro texture prewarming targets pages associated with long loading stalls in device logs.
  • Device validation is still needed. Synchronized eviction may introduce short transition pauses; translated data that changes texture-page layout also needs checking.

Chapter 5

Flowey video

  • Added pacing for the 24 FPS video and corrected the orientation of the host-screen blit.
  • Audio transition hold is released when the first video frame is presented, with active streams resumed explicitly.
  • End-of-file handling preserves the last frame while the scripted fade, pause and resume sequence finishes.
  • These changes are implemented, but audio synchronization, orientation and the complete ending still need a new device test. The video is not marked as fully fixed.

Final battle performance

  • Intermediate surfaces use a compact format to reduce graphics-memory pressure.
  • Added a Vita-specific lightweight shd_tower, reducing expensive per-pixel calculations and texture samples while retaining rotation, height, scale, front/back behavior and color blending.
  • Tower surface reuse on alternate frames remains in place.
  • The lightweight shader approximates the original appearance, especially at the cylinder edges. Its visual quality and FPS improvement are not yet confirmed on the Vita. Earlier device tests still reached only approximately 3–5 FPS in the critical scene.

[!WARNING] I'm trying to implement the shd_tower, this version might still run worse than the previous one (v0.74).

Known issues

  • GPU stability with Modern-GL + shaders ON still needs device confirmation in the minigame, Castle Town shop and other transitions.
  • Flowey video audio/finalization and final battle performance remain under validation.
  • Garden petal presentation and the intended Garden border fade-in remain unresolved or awaiting final validation.
  • Duplicated TP presentation in the Garden battle remains open. Logs show one tension-bar instance and one view; surface composition is still under investigation.
  • Garden battles and other heavy scenes can still have severe FPS drops or loading stalls.

Assets / Installation

  1. Just Install Deltarune-v0.75.Internal-Build-Test.vpk with VitaShell or FMVita.
  2. Keep your prepared game data and matching texture caches.
  3. For this version, simply use the same files generated by v0.73.

Testing / bug reports

Please use the Issues page. Include the build number, chapter, room, language, renderer, shader setting, texture-compression mode and relevant butterscotch-probe.log.

Official commercial DELTARUNE game data, music and Chapter video files are not distributed with this release.

ViTube

ViTube v2.0
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlive
v2.0 2026-09-15 07:45 UTC PSVitaAlive: 2.0
PSVitaAlive 2.0

ViTube 2.0 — hardware decoder no longer needs a system-wide plugin

Fixes #2 and #5 (VitaDB and Green Vita crashing after ViTube): ViTube bundled reAvPlayer.suprx (SonicMastr's ReAvPlayer), a taiHEN plugin that patched five syscall stubs inside SceAvcodecUser, a module every process on the console shares. When ViTube was closed from the LiveArea, the process was killed and the plugin's cleanup never ran, so the patches stayed in place and crashed the next app that touched the hardware H.264 decoder — until the console was rebooted.

The plugin is gone. The decoder now calls sceAvcdecDecodeAuInternal and sceAvcdecDecodeGetPictureWithWorkPictureInternal directly — the same pair the plugin's hook used to redirect to — so nothing outside ViTube's own process is touched anymore.

If you're updating from 1.2 or earlier, reboot the console once after installing. ViTube 2.0 itself doesn't need it, but a hook left behind by an older ViTube session survives until the next reboot regardless of which version replaces it.

No changes to playback quality, sign-in or networking. Saved settings stay valid.

Install

Download ViTube.vpk and install it with VitaShell (requires HENkaku/Ensō). Existing installs are updated in place. The corresponding source for this build (GPL-3.0 §6) is this repository at tag v2.0.

Plants vs. Zombies 2 for PS Vita — 1.1 RC12

RC12 fixes reproduced texture upload and allocation-recovery defects:

  • Correct mip handling for resized textures and placeholders.
  • Consistent RGBA8 storage and conversion for packed 4444/565 texture updates.
  • Checked recovery after failed alpha uploads or CPU downsampling.
  • Avoids retrying a larger allocation after a smaller one already failed.
  • Reports unrecoverable graphics-memory failure instead of continuing with resized render targets or failed placeholder storage.

Install pvz2-vita-latest.vpk over the existing version. Keep your game files and userdata/; no game data replacement is required.

Six regression cases fail against RC11 and pass against RC12. Compiled ARM checks verify the storage/update pixel bytes and the prior timezone fix; shader lifetime and pixel-worker checks also pass. No Vita3K was used.

The new RC11 log contains four texture allocation errors and reaches 189600 frames. Both supplied crash dumps are duplicates of older timezone crashes. These fixes are verified in isolated tests, but the reported latest crash is not conclusively identified and RC12 hardware confirmation is pending. Placeholder recovery may omit artwork. If graphics allocation cannot recover, the app reports an error and must be relaunched. Busy-scene FPS drops remain.

For a recurring crash, retain the newly generated dump and ux0:data/pvz2/userdata/loader.log before relaunching, plus stall.log if present. Include the build ID and the world/level/menu action.

Asphalt 8 Vita v0.3
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlive
v0.3 2026-09-11 02:10 UTC PSVitaAlive: 0.3
PSVitaAlive 0.3

Asphalt 8 Vita v0.3

This update improves race loading, reduces shader-related pauses and adds further stability and compatibility fixes. Your existing game files, saves and settings remain compatible.

Improvements

  • Fewer shader-related pauses. Bundled shader programs cover shared track and vehicle effects from their first use, with broader coverage for equivalent variants used throughout the game.
  • More reliable shader reuse. Fixed a cache-length issue that could cause a complete cached program to be rejected and compiled again.
  • Faster race loading. Race loading shares the OBB directory data between active scans instead of repeatedly reading the same large directory.
  • Loading recovery. Added targeted recovery for a stalled loading stage that could prevent the game from finishing a load after time spent idle.
  • Audio compatibility. Improved PCM sample-rate handling and read-only Vox state queries, avoiding unnecessary waits in those queries.
  • Further session-stability fixes. Improved cleanup of the game's thread synchronization objects when their memory is freed, and synchronized shader program deletion with outstanding GPU work.
  • Broader shader compatibility. Improved handling of shaders that exceed the usual varying slots, plus validation and serialization of cached programs.
  • Clearer setup errors. An APK size mismatch now names the supported v2.0.0e APK instead of referring to an internal development build.
  • Updated presentation. Includes the new bubble icon and LiveArea artwork.
  • Easier Windows setup. File pickers and a guided USB or PC-folder option handle file preparation and verification. FTP remains available.

The update retains traffic, breakables, collision behavior, car damage, particles and the existing graphics presets.

The recurring in-race pauses improved in Tokyo, Iceland and Nevada testing. Bundled programs cover their matching effects on first use, including the first run of a new installation. Effects outside that coverage still use the normal shader compiler; this is not a promise of hitch-free play on every track.

Updating

Install the new VPK over your existing installation. Keep your game-data folder and saves; there is no need to copy the APK/OBB again or clear the shader cache.

Known issues

  • The pause when finishing a race remains
  • Heavy scenes can still slow down; 60 FPS and hitch-free play are not guaranteed
  • Premium-currency cars, car packs, online services and gyro steering remain unavailable
  • Only the exact supported Android v2.0.0e game files are supported

Downloads

  • Install package — playable VPK, guided Windows setup, and instructions.
  • Source ZIP — source snapshot with its integrity manifest. Building is optional.
  • SHA-256 checksums.

Supply your own exact supported v2.0.0e APK and OBB. See installation instructions, compatibility, and shader provenance.

Due to Nate's current absence, Dogo and I will be making releases from this point onward (until Nate returns).

Parity Changes

  • Fixed volume of new sounds not being set correctly
  • Fixed missing input resets on some C blocks
  • Fixed clones being able to call threads after being deleted

Runtime Changes

  • Optimized collision

3DS/DS Changes

  • Improved SVG quality in dual screen mode

Vita RomM v0.8.0.s

First public test release of Vita RomM.

Vita RomM is a PS Vita homebrew client for browsing a self-hosted RomM library and downloading your own backed-up games directly on the Vita.

Features

  • Browse RomM platforms directly on PS Vita.
  • View games with cached cover art.
  • Download and install PS Vita game archives.
  • Download PSP games for Adrenaline.
  • Download PSX .bin/.cue sets and PSX EBOOT.PBP games.
  • Download common retro ROMs into configured emulator folders.
  • Show downloaded/installed status where supported.
  • Refresh LiveArea from inside the app.
  • Refresh cached cover art with Select.

Supported platforms

  • PS Vita
  • PSP
  • PSX / PlayStation
  • Game Boy Advance
  • Game Boy
  • Game Boy Color
  • NES
  • SNES
  • Sega Mega Drive / Genesis
  • Nintendo 64 experimental
  • Custom RomM platforms with configured paths

Setup

  1. Install vita_romm.vpk with VitaShell.
  2. Launch Vita RomM once.
  3. Edit:
    ux0:data/vita-romm/config.txt
  4. Set your RomM server URL and API token: server_url=http://your-romm-server.local/ api_token=rmm_your_token_here

See README.md for the full configuration guide.

Skyrift v1.3.0 — by Onur Kuru. Bug fixes, real difficulty, story beats, and a full visual pass.

Download skyrift.vpk below and install with VitaShell (X → Install). Requires a homebrew-enabled Vita. Desktop players can build from source (see the README).

Fixed

  • Void-fall "penalty" used to heal instead of hurt (subtracted 1 AFTER a full heal) - it's now capped at the HP you actually fell with, never a free heal, still never lethal
  • Stomp now always one-shots non-boss enemies - isle 6+ eagles at 4 HP (breed bonus) used to survive a stomp, breaking the taught "land on foes to squash them" rule
  • Fixed a frog telegraph animation desync on late isles, a three-part lightning lifecycle bug (bolts during death fades, frozen through hit-stop, popping across pause), and sparse weather at isle start
  • weather/difficulty tables moved into the generated level config instead of hard-coded level indices in the engine - reordering isles can no longer silently misattach them

New: difficulty & reward

  • Rift-touched eagles (isles 9-10) telegraph a dive attack: a hover-flash warning, then a fast dive at wherever you're standing
  • FLAWLESS bonus: clear an isle with every gem and zero damage for +500 score - now tracked live in the HUD, not just revealed at the door

New: story

  • A short lore beat between each of isles 2-10, setting up what's ahead

New: visuals

  • Hero: a dash streak pose and a hit-recoil tilt
  • Enemies: elite auras now breathe instead of a flat glow; bosses go visibly enraged below 1/3 HP (bigger glow, red fury flicker)
  • Environment: haze and god rays now match the isle's weather - cool moonlight through the firefly hollows, grey overcast in the storm, molten orange over the embers
  • HUD: the dash cooldown pip is labeled

24 automated tests, all 10 isles physics-verified reachable and soak-tested clean. Code is MIT © Onur Kuru. Art is Ansimuz's CC0 "Sunny Land" packs.

Barony Vita

Barony Vita v0.0.2-5.0.2
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlive
v0.0.2-5.0.2 2026-09-05 19:58 UTC PSVitaAlive: v.0.0.2-5.0.2
PSVitaAlive v.0.0.2-5.0.2

Barony Vita v0.0.2

Online multiplayer, a global leaderboard, achievements, and a batch of fixes.

Online multiplayer

  • Host or join games over the internet through the community master server, with automatic NAT traversal and a relay fallback when a direct connection fails.
  • Local ad-hoc play, and LAN over Wi-Fi, no router or internet needed.
  • Set a room password when hosting.
  • In-progress online games are saved for the next time your party plays together.

Global leaderboard

  • A worldwide board tied to your console, username set via settings page.
  • Your best run is submitted when you open the board, whether it came from single-player, an online game, or a save you are still playing.
  • Shows the top 20, and adds your own row at the bottom with your real rank when you are not in the top 20.
  • Every entry carries the full run: class, stats, cause of death, and the character's gear.

Online account

  • Your online identity and leaderboard progress live in one key file on the console: ux0:data/Barony/config/gossip_id.json.
  • Updating the game keeps it. Installing a newer VPK over your current install does not touch ux0:data/Barony, so your account, saves, and leaderboard entry all carry over.
  • Deleting that file, or wiping the game's save data, permanently unlinks your online account and its leaderboard entry. It cannot be recovered.
  • A fresh account is created automatically the next time you launch, and you set your name again. Reusing your old name may show as name#2, since the orphaned entry still holds the original.

Achievements

  • Achievements now track and unlock during play, saved on the console and online.

Fixes

  • Lighting: removed the rainbow specks along shadow edges, lifted pitch-black shadows so you can see in the dark (gamma slider), and smoothed the fade-to-black banding.
  • Enemies roam, infight, and give chase again instead of freezing at a distance. This also fixes bosses appearing without their body parts.
  • Torches and flames no longer drift or jitter.
  • Digging or breaking a wall no longer leaves a see-through gap.
  • Better handling when the console sleeps and wakes during a game.
  • Stability fixes across the math and lighting code.

Install

  • Download barony-blank.vpk and install it with VitaShell.
  • Barony's game files are not redistributable, so generate your own data from a PC copy and copy it to ux0:data/Barony on the Vita. See the README for the one-step tool.
  • Cross-play with PC is not supported. Play Vita to Vita.

Built from Barony 5.0.2. GPLv3.

Prince of Persia Classic

Prince of Persia Classic — PS Vita Port v01.28 - Full Control
↻ Pendiente PSVitaAlive
v01.28 2026-09-03 02:52 UTC PSVitaAlive: 01.20
PSVitaAlive 01.20 → release v01.28

Download & install

  1. Download popclassic.vpk from this release's assets.
  2. Install it with VitaShell on your PS Vita (running HENkaku/h-encore).
  3. Copy the game data to ux0:data/popclassic/ from your legally owned copy of the Android game. Full guide: INSTALL_HARDWARE.md

Upgrading? Same TITLEID (POPC00001) as every build since v01.10: installing over an older one keeps your saves. Coming from v01.20 or later, just install the .vpk — the data in ux0:data/popclassic/ is unchanged.

This repo contains no original game code, binaries or assets. Prince of Persia Classic is the intellectual property of Ubisoft Entertainment; you need your own legal copy of the Android game.

Controls

The game switches between "platform" and "combat" mode on its own (sword drawn or not), so several buttons do double duty.

Button Platform mode Combat mode
Left stick / D-Pad Move — tap for one careful step, hold to run same
Cross Jump Attack
Square Crouch Defend / parry
Triangle Interact (grab, levers) Sheath sword
Circle / Down Crouch —
Up Jump / climb —
Start Pause menu Pause menu
Select Menu Menu
L + R together Show/hide the on-screen touch buttons same
Touchscreen Still works for menu navigation —

[!IMPORTANT] Coming from v01.20 or earlier, two things changed:

  1. Square is no longer the "walk" modifier — it's crouch / defend now. Walking needs no modifier any more: tap for a step, hold to run.
  2. The D-Pad runs now. "D-Pad only walks, use the analog stick until it's fixed" was a known limitation from the very first build. It no longer applies.

What's new

🎮 Controls

  • You can jump while running. This was the reported bug that survived four attempted fixes. It was never an engine block: the synthetic-touch emulation couldn't express "run" and "jump" at once because they competed for finite touch slots.
  • Physical buttons use the game's own gamepad path. This port wraps the Xperia PLAY build, which ships full physical-gamepad support — and the port had never switched it on (it passed "PSVita" as the device name instead of "R800i", the Xperia PLAY's model number, since its first commit). Now it does: the touch buttons are hidden by the game's own code, menus get a D-Pad-navigable cursor, and tutorials describe physical buttons.
  • Walk vs. run uses the game's real rule (a 250 ms threshold), instead of the three invented mechanics tried before — distance-from-centre, double-tap, drag simulation — none of which worked.
  • Cross jumps again. v01.26 had concluded, with two functions inverted, that jump was control1Clicked — which is actually crouch.
  • Cross confirms in menus again, broken by the previous draft for as long as a game was loaded.
  • L+R toggle to hide the touch buttons, now without v01.25's bug that disabled walking.
  • Memory corruption fixed: the previous toggle wrote up to ~150 bytes past the end of an object every time it was used.

🩺 Diagnostics & stability

  • Live logs over Wi-Fi (UDP broadcast alongside the file): a session that ends in a crash or hard reset no longer loses its tail. ENABLE_VERBOSE_LOG=ON builds only.
  • Crash fixed when starting that network logger (the SceNet/SceNetCtl modules weren't being loaded).
  • vitaGL splashscreen can be disabled (NO_SPLASHSCREEN, on by default).

Still open

  • This release is untested on console. Most likely to need tuning: the 250 ms walk-to-run threshold.
  • Not compatible with Vita3K — an emulator bug, not a port bug (non-power-of-2 swizzled textures). This port targets real hardware.
  • Not using the game's original fonts: DejaVu Serif is used instead, for licensing reasons.

  • Controls reference for developers (ControlsLayer member layout, keycode → handler → event table, the CONTROL_EVENT bitmask, the walk→run rule): docs/comments/main.c.md

Hi everyone! Big update here, since I got my SD2Vita I have been doing a lot of optimization. I bumped the resolution of the Vita port to 480x272, so it is just a little bit more clearer, the HUD will always be Native resolution, so it doesn't become blurry. I added a optimizer, that let's you cache the textures before hand, which improves loading times substantially, this can be skipped, and only needs to be done once! I have made a lot of optimizations with the frame rate, and stutters. I will admit that the game is not smooth 30fps all the way through, but it is much better than it was at last release! Notable, audio, like the thunder, doesn't freeze the game for a good second, which you would notice right away at the start of the game, that is NO MORE. There is still quite a bit of work that could be done, and I wouldn't mind if anyone would like to contribute, feel free to make pull requests. I also added a updater for the Vita, which should check on startup if you have internet, if there is a new update, you can skip it if you like, it might need more testing and refining though.

QoL improvement, I have added Hint sizes, I noticed while testing a bit, I felt the hints could be a bit hard to read at it's original size, so I have added Hint sizes, this can be changed in the gameplay options, for the Vita it's default on Medium.

I have also made the port more accessible on Android, no longer requiring Vulkan 1.3, should work on Android devices that support Vulkan 1.1+

Full Changelog: https://github.com/FridiNaTor1/HPL2-handyman/compare/1.3...1.5

Planned features: Controller detection for Android and PC, where the controller glyphs change depending on which type of Controller you are using, automatically, and getting rid of Controller hints when you are using Keyboard and Mouse only! Improving the Vita control scheme, there is a part of the game where you should be using the directional button to do a puzzle, which is currently mapped incorrectly, sorry! Improving the Android control scheme, and make it aware of desktop mode, as in when you connect the phone to a TV, the game should take advantage of that, and remove the touch only control scheme, and be able to be played with Mouse and Keyboard, or a Controller. Better options for every platform, like keybinds/sensitivity, etc.

Known Issues: Android stutters, this will be looked into! Vita unstable FPS, yeah obviously, but it's a bit better now atleast! Android running is awkward, I'll try to make it better! Vita's inventory, pause menu, and journal, doesn't fade the background.

Battleship Vita

1.4 (PS Vita port)
↻ Pendiente PSVitaAlive
1.4 2026-08-31 17:23 UTC PSVitaAlive: v.1.0
PSVitaAlive v.1.0 → release 1.4

1.4 build of the PS Vita port (SSB64VITA).

Changelog since 1.3

Hi-res texture packs (new on Vita)

  • Texture-pack support now works on the Vita, same model as desktop/Android: extract a pack .zip into ux0:data/battleship/mods/ and it's read in place.
  • Vita decode path uses libpng straight into the texture cache (much faster than stb_image on the Vita CPU).
  • Vita-tuned memory limits: 32 MB decoded-texture LRU cache (gHiResTextures.CacheBudgetMB overrides), and a 1024×1024 per-texture cap — anything bigger transparently falls back to the native texture so one oversized upscale can't blow the budget.
  • Directory scan uses sceIoDread directly instead of std::filesystem (which returned EINVAL on some valid ux0: pack paths and aborted the whole scan).

Bundled texture packs

Three memory-tuned downscales of GhostlyDark's SSB Reloaded pack are attached to this release (and kept in-repo under mods/texture_pack/). Pick one and copy it, still zipped, to ux0:data/battleship/mods/:

Pack Scale Notes
texture_pack_1x.zip 1× lightest; only a marginal step up from native — not really worth it
texture_pack_1.5x.zip 1.5× recommended — sharper textures, no performance hit
texture_pack_2x.zip 2× sharpest, but visibly slows the system; only if you accept the frame-rate cost

Don't drop more than one in at once — every pack in mods/ is indexed and the last one scanned wins each texture, wasting memory.

Modding

  • Mod ABI v9: new fighter_special_hi_map(fighter_gobj, landing_lag) entry point — a generalized Mario-style special-up collision/cliff path so native fighter mods can supply their own landing lag while the host keeps collision and engine-transition ownership.

Netplay

  • Build id → 1.4. 1.4 clients only match other 1.4 clients; if you self-host the lobby board (server/matchmaker/), redeploy it — its default -build is now 1.4.

Full details: CHANGELOG.md

Requires

  • Your own copy of Super Smash Bros. (N64) US NTSC v1.0.
  • BattleShip.o2r extracted from your ROM, copied to ux0:data/battleship/BattleShip.o2r (see scripts/extract-vita-data.sh).

Install

Copy battleship.vpk to the Vita and install with VitaShell (or similar). First launch needs a few minutes to compile the shader cache — don't interrupt it.

Known gaps

  • 3–4 player netplay is not fully tested.
  • A console behind CGNAT (some fibre / mobile) can only join, not host — no relay yet.

Changelog

All notable changes to vitastremio (PS Vita Stremio client + middleware).

[1.3] - 2026-08-27

Update both halves. Reinstall the VPK and restart the middleware.

Fixed

Sound and picture drifting apart after about 35 minutes. Long films would play perfectly and then, always at roughly the same point, the picture would jump ahead of the sound and never settle again. The app was losing track of time once playback passed 35 minutes and 47 seconds, which is why it happened at the same moment every time. It now keeps time correctly for far longer than any film.

Added

A proper loading screen. Starting something used to show a black screen while it buffered, which was hard to tell apart from the app having frozen. You now get the film's artwork, its title, and a spinner while it gets ready.

Worth knowing

  • Artwork comes from your addons, so titles without it will show the title on a plain background instead. Nothing else changes.

PSVitaAlive v0.6.1 → release v0.6.2

FileManager Vita v0.6.2

This release focuses on stability, touch input and visual refinements.

Highlights

  • Added two color themes: Dark, with a black and dark-gray palette, and Pink, with hot-pink and light tones.
  • Refined Grid view with the standard font size, centered file/folder names and width-aware ellipsis for long names.
  • The dedicated Icons set is now always active and its redundant selector was removed from Settings.
  • Added Wi-Fi and Bluetooth status icons. They are shown only when the corresponding connection/feature is active.
  • Added touch input to controls that previously only displayed a button hint, including the OK button in file properties.
  • Single-item copy, move and delete dialogs now show the selected file/folder name; multi-item actions retain the compact count summary.

Stability fixes

  • Limited and periodically cleaned the Recent directory, removing stale entries to prevent excessive directory growth.
  • Added a five-second directory-read safeguard that returns to the default root when a directory stalls.
  • Fixed IME lifecycle and buffer handling issues that could crash rename/input operations.
  • Hardened VPK installation and progress-thread synchronization to prevent stalls around extraction and promotion.
  • Removed the GIF background from the VPK after identifying excessive decoded-frame memory use as a potential source of freezes during installation.
  • Fixed invalid touch routing while modal dialogs are open and other crash-prone edge cases found in collected logs.

Installation

Copy FileManager_v0.6.2.vpk to your PS Vita and install it with VitaShell or another VPK installer. HENkaku/h-encore is required.

Immortal Dusk Vita

Immortal Dusk — PS Vita Port v1.0
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlive
1.0 2026-08-21 21:50 UTC PSVitaAlive: v.1.0
PSVitaAlive v.1.0

⚔️ Immortal Dusk — PS Vita Port v1.0

First official release of Immortal Dusk for the PlayStation Vita and PlayStation TV!

This port brings Gamevil's classic action RPG to the PS Vita natively via dynamic ARM shared library loading (.so loader), FalsoJNI, and vitaGL hardware scaling.

✨ Features & Highlights

  • 🚀 Native 60 FPS Performance: Internal 800x480 RGB565 software rasterizer hardware-scaled to full screen (960x544) with bilinear filtering via vitaGL.
  • 🎮 Full Physical & Touch Controls: Complete dual-input support:
    • 8-direction movement via Left Analog Stick and D-Pad.
    • Face buttons and triggers mapped for fast combat, skills, and item shortcuts.
    • Full Front Touchscreen support for menus, inventory, and HUD navigation.
  • 🔊 Low-Latency Multi-Voice Audio Engine: Powered by sceAudioOut, supporting 12-voice polyphonic WAV PCM sound effects and memory-streamed looping MP3 background music (minimp3).
  • 💎 Offline Cash Shop & K-Point Emulation: Built-in local simulation of Gamevil's legacy server protocol, preventing infinite loading hangs and allowing purchases of potions, resurrection stones, teleport scrolls, and bag/storage expansions completely offline.
  • 🖼️ High-Quality LiveArea: Custom icon, startup gate, and background remastered with 8-bit indexed palettes matching PS Vita OS standards.

🕹️ Controls

PS Vita Button In-Game Action
Left Stick / D-Pad 8-Direction Character Movement
Cross ($\times$) Primary Attack / Talk / Confirm
Square ($\square$) Skill 1
Triangle ($\triangle$) Skill 2
Circle ($\bigcirc$) Skill 3 / Cancel / Back
R1 Trigger Skill 4
L1 Trigger Quick HP Potion
SELECT Quick MP Potion
START In-Game Menu / Pause
Front Touchscreen Direct touch interaction across menus, inventory, and HUD

📦 Requirements & Installation Guide

Legal Disclaimer: This release only provides the loader executable (.vpk). No copyrighted assets or proprietary binaries are included. You must supply files from a legally acquired copy of Immortal Dusk v1.0.2 for Android.

1. Prerequisites on your PS Vita

Ensure you have the following plugins installed:

  • kubridge.skprx
  • fd_fix.skprx (or rePatch)
  • libshacccg.suprx (installed in ur0:data/ via ShaRKBR3ED or CrystalPSM)

2. Setup Steps

  1. Download and install immortal_dusk.vpk on your PS Vita using VitaShell.
  2. Obtain your legal Immortal Dusk_1.0.2.apk file and rename/extract it as a .zip archive.
  3. Extract and copy the following files to ux0:data/immortaldusk/:
    • Copy lib/armeabi/libaist-jni.so $\to$ ux0:data/immortaldusk/libaist-jni.so
    • Copy the APK's assets/ folder $\to$ ux0:data/immortaldusk/assets/
    • Copy the APK's res/raw/ folder $\to$ ux0:data/immortaldusk/res/raw/

📂 Final Folder Structure on ux0:

ux0:data/immortaldusk/
├── libaist-jni.so
├── assets/
│   ├── ani_data/
│   ├── data/
│   ├── font/
│   ├── img/
│   ├── txt/
│   └── txte/
├── res/
│   └── raw/
│       ├── snd0.wav ... snd61.wav
│       └── snd100.mp3 ... snd122.mp3
└── saves/
  1. Launch the game from your LiveArea and enjoy!

  • TheFloW for the .so loader architecture and kubridge.
  • Rinnegatamante for vitaGL and invaluable contributions to the PS Vita scene.
  • Volodymyr Atamanenko for so_util and soloader boilerplate.

Cordless

Cordless v1.0.0
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlive
v1.0.0 2026-08-20 03:07 UTC PSVitaAlive: v.1.0.0
PSVitaAlive v.1.0.0

Cordless 1.0.0

A native Discord client for the PlayStation Vita. It talks straight to Discord over TLS, so there's no bridge server and nothing to self-host.

Features

  • Servers, DMs, group DMs, and threads
  • Send, edit, reply, react, and forward; scroll up to load history
  • Images, GIFs, WebP, and video / voice-message playback
  • Emoji, live presence, typing indicators, friends, and profile popouts
  • Join by invite, block users, and multiple accounts
  • Settings: light/dark theme, accent color, font size, compact mode, 12/24h clock, and a low-battery mode

Voice channels are still a work in progress and are turned off in this build.

Logging in

No password either way. Two options:

  • QR code: scan the on-screen code with the official Discord mobile app. It's the quick path, but Discord sometimes asks for a captcha during QR sign-in that the Vita can't complete. If that happens, use the token method.
  • Token: put your Discord user token on the card once. The full walkthrough (a one-click bookmarklet, the browser Network tab, or by hand) is in docs/login.md. (https://github.com/Brendonm17/Cordless/blob/main/docs/login.md)

Terms of service

Using a user token with a third-party client is against Discord's Terms of Service. Cordless is built for personal use and interoperability, not automation, and you run it on your own account at your own risk. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Discord or Sony.

AI was used for API research and live area assets.

Install

  1. A Vita or PS TV on HENkaku / h-encore2 (firmware 3.60 to 3.74) with unsafe homebrew enabled.
  2. Copy Cordless.vpk to the Vita and install it in VitaShell.
  3. Launch it, then follow docs/login.md to add your token.

Logs are written to ux0:data/cordless/log.txt.

Vitabright Lut Editor

VitaBrightEX v1.3 + LUT Editor v4.2
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlive
v1.3 2026-08-18 09:10 UTC PSVitaAlive: v.4.2
PSVitaAlive v.4.2

VitaBrightEX v1.3 + LUT Editor v4.2

Critical fixes in this release

OLED: presets no longer destroy screen colours

The previous OLED screen filter applied CCT/gamma/contrast math directly to the panel's 21-byte LUT rows. Those bytes are panel hardware control registers — not linear RGB pixel values. Applying a colour matrix to them produced wrong results and made every single preset look worse than the default. This is now fully fixed.

The OLED LUT is left completely untouched by the filter system. Your screen colour is set by the calibrated per-panel LUT file (vitabright_lut_p5.txt etc.) loaded at boot — which already has the correct white-point for your specific panel. Factory reset restores this clean state instantly.

Tab switching now works reliably

The app was using sceCtrlPeekBufferPositiveExt2 which remaps the physical L/R shoulder buttons to different bit positions (L1/R1 DS4 style) that the code wasn't reading. Fixed: uses plain sceCtrlPeekBufferPositive so the physical L/R buttons correctly switch tabs.

What each part now does

Plugin v1.3

  • OLED colour is controlled by the per-panel LUT file only
  • Filter math (CCT/gamma/contrast) is NOT applied to OLED — it was the wrong architecture and destroyed calibration
  • Hardware invert (sceDisplaySetInvertColorsForDriver) still works
  • LCD filter (IFTU CSC matrix) unchanged — works correctly

App v4.2 on Vita 1000 (OLED):

  • Tab 1: Invert toggle + Factory reset — the only safe options
  • Tab 2: Invert only, with explanation of why CCT/gamma/contrast are not shown (to prevent accidentally breaking colours)

App v4.2 on Vita 2000 (LCD):

  • Tab 1: Full CCT preset list (6500K–1200K) + IPS/sRGB/Night/Boost enhancements — correct because IFTU CSC applies to pixel data
  • Tab 2: Temperature / Gamma / Contrast / Brightness / Invert sliders

Factory reset (Triangle): Calls vitabrightOledReload() to restore the clean panel LUT from the panel-specific file on disk, then clears invert. Restores original colours immediately without a reboot.

Installation

  1. Extract VitaBrightEX-v1.3.zip and copy all files to ur0:/tai/
  2. Add ur0:/tai/vitabright.skprx under *KERNEL in ur0:/tai/config.txt
  3. Reboot
  4. Install VitaBrightEX-LUT-Editor-v4.2.vpk via VitaShell

If ux0:/tai/ exists on your memory card it takes priority over ur0:/tai/.

Based on vitabright by devnoname120 (https://github.com/devnoname120/vitabright). Screen filter inspired by Luma3DS Rosalina (https://github.com/LumaTeam/Luma3DS).

⚔️ Zenonia 4 — PlayStation Vita Port (v1.0.0)

First official release of the native Zenonia 4 (Android) port for the PlayStation Vita, featuring intelligent multi-tier FrameSkip, direct RGB565 hardware rendering, RAM audio caching, and maximum CPU optimization.

🚀 What's New in v1.0.0

  • ⚡ Multi-Tier FrameSkip (1.0x to 3.0x):
    • Dynamic frame pacing allowing you to adjust game speed in real-time between 1.0x (Normal), 1.5x, 2.0x (Default), 2.5x, and 3.0x (Max).
    • Game logic, physics, enemy AI, and touch/pad inputs run at a full 60 Hz tick rate while rendering load is cut down, yielding a super-smooth 20–30+ FPS experience.
    • Frame pacing is active across gameplay, Title screen animations, and Main Menus.
  • 🖥️ On-Screen OSD HUD Notification:
    • Displays a clean, translucent banner at the top of the screen when changing speed modes (FRAME SKIP: 2.0X, etc.) with smooth fade-out.
  • 🛡️ 100% Authentic Visuals & UI Bug Fixes:
    • Off-screen text and button caches (p9 != 0) are fully preserved, fixing missing text labels on pause/inventory popups (Destroy, Repair, Equip, Discard).
    • Redundant 1.04 MB FastClearNonClipping writes are bypassed on skipped frames to drastically reduce RAM bandwidth usage.
  • 🔇 Zero-Log Max CPU Performance:
    • Release binaries are built with file logging disabled (ENABLE_LOGGING=OFF), eliminating SD card / SD2Vita write latency and format-string overhead during gameplay.
  • 🎵 Multi-Core Thread Affinity:
    • Main game loop pinned to CPU Core 0 at 444 MHz.
    • Audio mixing and background OGG playback isolated to CPU Core 1 with zero SD card access (audio cached in RAM).

🎮 Controls

Button / Input Action
D-Pad / Left Stick Move character / Navigate menus
Cross (✕) Attack / Confirm / Interact
Circle (◯) Back / Cancel
Triangle (△) Skip dialogue / Cutscene
Square (□) Open World Map
L-Trigger Quick Save Game
R-Trigger + SELECT Cycle FrameSkip Speed (1.0x ➔ 1.5x ➔ 2.0x ➔ 2.5x ➔ 3.0x)
START + SELECT Exit Game safely
Front Touchscreen Full native touch controls & menu navigation

📦 Installation Instructions

  1. Install zenonia_4.vpk on your PlayStation Vita via VitaShell.
  2. Extract the game asset files from the Android APK (assets/ and lib/armeabi/libgameDSO.so) into ux0:data/zenonia-4/.
  3. Ensure ux0:data/zenonia-4/libgameDSO.so and ux0:data/zenonia-4/assets/ are present.
  4. Launch Zenonia 4 from LiveArea and enjoy the game!

📁 Downloads / Assets

  • zenonia_4.vpk: Standard build with Multi-Tier FrameSkip, Maximum CPU speed, zero SD card I/O.

Minecraft: Story Mode

MCSM Vita 1.11 — Public Prerelease
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlivePRE-RELEASE
v1.11 2026-08-12 11:39 UTC PSVitaAlive: v.1.11
PSVitaAlive v.1.11

MCSM 1.11 — public prerelease

[!IMPORTANT] This is a fix pass, not a confirmed-working pass. Everything below was traced from code, disassembly, or a device loader.log and fixed on that basis — none of it has been confirmed by a full playthrough yet. In particular, this release does not claim choices or settings now save correctly; it describes the specific mechanisms that were found broken and what changed. If a problem persists, the logging build exists to find out why instead of guessing again.

The VPK on this release is a LOGGING build (MCSM-1.11-logging.vpk). It writes a diagnostic log to ux0:data/mcsm/loader.log while you play, and it runs slower than a normal build because of it — please don't report its framerate as a performance bug. A non-logging build (MCSM-1.11.vpk) is also attached.

How to send a log

  1. Play until the problem happens.
  2. Close the game. If it is frozen: press PS, then close it from the LiveArea.
  3. Do not launch the game again yet — the log is wiped at the start of every launch, so relaunching destroys what you just captured.
  4. Copy ux0:data/mcsm/loader.log off the Vita — open VitaShell, press SELECT to start its FTP server, and copy the file from a PC.
  5. Attach it to a bug report or post it in the Discord. Zip it if it is large.

To turn logging off without changing builds, create an empty ux0:data/mcsm/settings/nolog.txt.

Use Data Builder v1.9 (unchanged from 1.10 — same file, reused as-is).

This release contains the PS Vita loader with community LiveArea artwork and trophy support, the Windows data builder, and the corresponding source code. It does not contain the Android APK, OBBs, episodes, native game libraries, or gameplay archives.

Questions, test results, and bug reports are welcome in the MCSM Vita Discord.

Downloads

  • MCSM-1.11-logging.vpk — complete Vita loader, logging build (see the box above); install with VitaShell.
  • MCSM-1.11.vpk — the same loader without logging, for normal play once a problem is no longer being chased.
  • MCSM-Vita-Data-Builder-v1.9.exe — unchanged from 1.10; builds ux0:data/mcsm or a chapter-only copy pack from your legally owned Android files.

What changed in this pass

  • Preference load ran before its resource could exist. SavePrefs was writing correctly the whole time; the load that reads it back now retries once the resource it needs is actually registered, instead of only trying once, too early, at boot.
  • Found and fixed a real bug in the shipped engine's event log, not a porting artifact: on a missing anchor event, DeleteAllEventsAfterEvent underflows to a full-log wipe instead of doing nothing. SaveLoad_Load calls the vulnerable path on every load; it's now guarded against exactly that case.
  • The post-save mirror was guessing which copy the engine wrote, and guessed wrong — from the second save onward it silently overwrote every save with the first one's contents. It now checks which copy actually changed instead of assuming.
  • Save writes are now staged and size-verified before being committed by rename, and a one-generation backup restores a save that's provably too small to be intact.
  • Audio mixer was writing into a buffer the hardware was still playing, audible as tearing in busy scenes with several NPCs on screen; it now rotates through buffers that were already allocated but unused.
  • The virtual controller could be dropped by the system around common dialogs (trophy setup, the rename keyboard) and never came back, leaving only touch controls; it's now checked and re-added automatically.
  • The 30fps cap allowed a fast frame through right after a slow one; presents are now floored against the actual previous present so the display can't exceed the configured cap.
  • An animation-timing repair forced a quarter-second jump on every scene load, not just on the hitches it was meant to smooth; it now treats a load as a pause (nothing to catch up to) rather than lost time.
  • The save-rename on-screen keyboard could show leftover characters from a previous rename on top of the new one; its input buffer is now cleared between uses.
  • New LiveArea icon and content-screen artwork.

Data Builder v1.9

Unchanged from the 1.10 release.

Inotia 3: Children of Carnia — PS Vita Port v1.0.0

First official release of the native Android-to-PS Vita wrapper port for Inotia 3: Children of Carnia (originally by Com2uS). Powered by so-loader, FalsoJNI, and vitaGL.

The game has been thoroughly reverse-engineered and tested on physical PS Vita hardware and is fully playable from start to finish.

🌟 Key Features & Improvements

  • Fully Playable Offline Campaign: Complete story mode, party management, skills, inventory, map transitions, and combat are 100% functional.
  • Native 960x544 Visuals: Fullscreen hardware rendering via vitaGL (OpenGL ES 1.1 fixed-function pipeline with custom GL_FIXED to GL_FLOAT array conversion and GL_LINEAR texture filtering).
  • Dual Control Support: Full physical button mapping (D-Pad, Left Analog Stick, Face Buttons, Triggers) alongside multi-touch front touchscreen support.
  • Native Audio Engine: Music and SFX decoded directly via Tremor / libogg portlibs.
  • Reliable Save System: Save files persist directly in ux0:data/inotia3/save<N>.dat.
  • Game Engine Bypasses: Bypassed anti-tamper security routines (excuteDirectly, jIsCracked) and stuck ad-loop transitions (Extend_CheckAdvDisplay).

📋 Prerequisites & Requirements

Before installing, ensure your PS Vita has:

  1. Custom Firmware (3.60 / 3.65 Enso recommended).
  2. Plugins installed in ur0:tai/config.txt under *KERNEL:
    • kubridge.skprx (v0.3 or newer)
    • fd_fix.skprx (or rePatch)
  3. libshacccg.suprx installed in ur0:data/ (can be extracted using ShaRKBR33D).

📦 Installation Guide

  1. Install inotia3.vpk on your PS Vita using VitaShell.
  2. Legally obtain a copy of the Inotia 3: Children of Carnia Android APK (v1.3.2).
  3. Open the .apk using any zip extractor (like 7-Zip).
  4. Copy lib/armeabi/libgame.so to:
    ux0:data/inotia3/libgame.so
  5. Extract the assets/ folder from the .apk and copy its contents to:
    ux0:data/inotia3/assets/
    (Or copy extracted game resources into ux0:data/inotia3/assets/common/game_res/)
  6. Launch the game from LiveArea!

Zenonia 3

Zenonia 3 PS Vita - v01.30 - Externalized Assets & Optimized Default Build
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlive
v01.30 2026-07-24 00:27 UTC PSVitaAlive: v.1.30
PSVitaAlive v.1.30

Description

This release brings important changes to how the game's UI assets are loaded to reduce the footprint of the VPK, and establishes the most stable graphical configuration as the default build.

⚠️ Important Installation Change (Action Required)

The UI assets (menu art, title logos, and HELP/ABOUT text) are no longer bundled within the VPK. You must now manually copy these folders from your legally obtained .apk to your PS Vita during the installation process:

  1. Extract res/drawable/ from your APK, rename it to drawable, and place it in ux0:data/zenonia3/drawable/
  2. Extract assets/html/ from your APK, rename it to html, and place it in ux0:data/zenonia3/html/

Note: Without these files, the game will still run, but menus, titles, and help screens will render completely blank.

What's New

  • Optimized Default Build: The project now defaults to the most stable performance settings confirmed on real hardware (RGB565_CONVERT_MODE=NATIVE, OPTIMIZE_NEON_FIXED=OFF, and LOCK_FPS_30=ON). The standard build output is now a clean zenonia_3.vpk instead of a long, heavily tagged filename.
  • Developer Workflow Improvements: Added new options in the Python management scripts to quickly upload only the eboot.bin` over FTP, allowing for much faster iterative testing without needing to repack and reinstall the entire VPK.
  • New Porting Utilities: Added new developer tools (parse_dump.py and ai_bash_commands.sh) to the repository to assist in parsing PS Vita crash dumps and streamlining the porting workflow.

Why are some previous releases missing a .vpk file?

In earlier stages of this project, a bad practice was inadvertently being followed: distributing .vpk files that had copyrighted game assets (such as UI graphics, title logos, and menus) bundled directly inside them. Distributing copyrighted material without authorization is a violation of copyright laws and could have severely compromised this entire open-source repository, potentially leading to a DMCA takedown.

To protect the repository and ensure the longevity of this port, we have strictly pivoted away from this practice. No copyrighted assets will ever be bundled with our releases moving forward. This is why the loader logic has been updated to completely externalize these assets, requiring users to manually extract and provide them from their own legally obtained copies of the game.

We appreciate your understanding and cooperation in keeping this project safe, legal, and compliant.

⬇ zenonia_3.vpk · 1.6 MB

Zenonia 2

Zenonia 2: The Lost Memories - PS Vita Port v1.2.0: Major Performance & Stability Overhaul
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlive
v1.20 2026-07-18 03:31 UTC PSVitaAlive: v.1.20
PSVitaAlive v.1.20

Description

This release focuses entirely on performance and stability. Previously the game had an unstable framerate, no VSync, and a hard, noticeable frame drop every time a hit landed in combat — all of that is fixed here. The audio and rendering hot paths were reworked at a lower level, and the framerate is now capped and VSync'd for a consistent, tear-free experience.

What's New:

• Fixed Combat Freezes: Sound effects no longer block the game's render loop. Previously, every time a sound played (e.g. a hit landing) it opened and decoded the audio file directly on the main thread — that work now happens asynchronously on the audio thread, eliminating the FPS spikes that happened on every collision/hit. • Optimized Video Pipeline: The internal pixel conversion needed every frame for the game's software-rendered screen no longer allocates/frees memory per frame, and is now NEON-accelerated, cutting its CPU cost significantly with no visible quality loss. • Stable ~30 FPS with Real VSync: Framerate is now capped to the game's original target (~30 FPS) with VSync enabled — no more screen tearing, and the game no longer runs faster than it was designed to. • Reduced Logging Overhead: Removed several always-on debug logs that were silently writing to disk on every asset check during actual gameplay (not just at boot), and registered a couple of previously unimplemented engine callbacks (vibration, etc.) so it stops repeatedly retrying failed lookups. • CPU/GPU Clock Boost (carried over): CPU/bus/GPU clocks are set to their safe maximum at startup, since the engine composites every frame in software. • For developers: added a reusable porting_tools/ toolkit (build/deploy/debug helpers) generalized from this port.

Known Issues (unchanged): • Logo/title screens may appear blank until you tap the touchscreen to advance. • The experimental post-process shader build may show a black screen after the menu — use the standard VPK if this happens.

Installation Note: No changes to the install layout in this release — if you're upgrading from v1.1.0, just replace the VPK.

GMCA

GMCA v1.1.0
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlive
v1.1.0 2026-07-17 12:13 UTC PSVitaAlive: v1.1.0
PSVitaAlive v1.1.0

Added

  • Stremio: external subtitles from a subtitles addon (#51). When your Stremio account has a subtitles addon installed (e.g. OpenSubtitles), its tracks now show up in the player's subtitle menu, resolved on demand at playback time. Resolution runs off the UI thread so it never delays the start of a stream, and the hook is a no-op for Plex and Jellyfin, which already expose their own subtitle tracks. A hint is shown when no subtitles addon is configured, so the empty menu is not mistaken for a bug.

Fixed

  • PS Vita: the remaining GPU crashes ("blue light of death"), offline and in the music/overview screens. Following 1.0.5's Stremio artwork fix, three further GPU-memory exhaustion paths on the Vita's tiny CDRAM were closed:
    • Texture memory is now bounded overall. A hard byte cap on the image cache stops the overview and music grids from stacking enough textures to fault the allocator mid-render.
    • Offline/cached artwork was still uploaded at full resolution. It is now downscaled to the display size on GXM like online artwork, fixing the crash that only reproduced offline (#60).
    • The mpv video FBO no longer requests MSAA, freeing ~6 MB of CDRAM during playback (#61).
    • The mpv GXM FBO init is now guarded, and Stremio sources the Vita decoder cannot handle are skipped instead of crashing.
  • Stremio: debrid/Torrentio config changes did not take effect (#46). The account's addon collection is now re-synced at startup, so reconfiguring Torrentio (e.g. wiring up AllDebrid or changing filters) is picked up on the next launch instead of keeping the stale addon set.
  • Music: the artist page crashed on Switch + Jellyfin when navigating up from the header with the D-pad (#44).
  • Music: the album screen showed an inaccurate loading skeleton that did not match the real content layout.
  • Connection: remote (WAN) reconnects were slow or failed (#36). Server candidates are now raced in parallel instead of tried one at a time, so the first reachable address wins.
  • Connection: the connection tiles now respond to a tap (touch/mouse), not only to the gamepad.
  • Desktop: crash and misplaced widgets where no battery or wi-fi info is available (#37). The battery widget is hidden on PC desktop, and both the battery and wireless widgets now guard their draw() against missing platform info (fixes a Linux desktop crash).
  • Offline downloads now run on a thread pool, keeping the UI responsive and cleaning up their HTTP sessions correctly.
  • Focus: a freshly built list now defaults focus to the lowest-index cell rather than whichever cell was inserted first.

Build

  • Bumped mbedTLS 3.6.5-1 → 3.6.7-1 for the Vita and Switch builds.

Sonic Robo Blast 2 Kart

SRB2Kart for PS Vita / PS TV — v2.1 (DualShock rumble)
✓ Al día en PSVitaAlive
v2.1 2026-07-14 18:14 UTC PSVitaAlive: 2.1
PSVitaAlive 2.1

Rumble. A DualShock 3/4 plugged into a PS TV has motors — the port now uses them.

Event Feel
Bumping another kart short thump
Spinout (banana, orbinaut…) medium shake
Squish (Grow/Shrink) heavier
Explosion (mine, SPB, Eggman) full strength
Boost / sneaker 2 s of high-frequency buzz
Offroad (grass, sand, mud) continuous grind, scaled by how deep the offroad is and how fast you are actually ploughing through it

Set it in Options → Controls → Gamepad Options → Rumble — Off / Light / Normal / Strong (default: Normal).

Splitscreen rumbles the right controller: SDL's Vita backend maps each pad to its own port. On a handheld Vita there are no motors, so the feature is simply inert — nothing to turn off, nothing to break. It cannot desync online play either: the rumble code only ever reads player state.

Which VPK do I download?

srb2kart-modern-vitagl.vpk srb2kart-2019-vitagl.vpk
Rumble ✅ new in v2.1 ❌ (unchanged from v2.0)
vitaGL latest upstream the 2019 version (srb2-vita)
Change resolution live, no restart requires a restart
Extra file on the console yes — libshacccg.suprx none
Source branch vitagl-modern (default) master

Only the modern build changed in v2.1. srb2kart-2019-vitagl.vpk is the exact same file as in v2.0 — re-attached so this release stands on its own. Rumble was not backported to it because it has not been tested on that branch.

⚠️ Install only one at a time. Both use the same title ID (SRB2KART0), so installing one replaces the other. Your data in ux0:data/srb2kart/ is kept either way.

Updating from v2.0

Install the VPK over the old one with VitaShell. Your game data and settings are kept, and rumble defaults to Normal on first launch.

Full install instructions, controls and build notes: README.

Credits

SRB2Kart by Kart Krew. PS Vita/PS TV port built on the work of Rinnegatamante (srb2-vita, vitaGL) with help from Ryo. Ported by Esod.

vitaMania! v0.1.0a

A PS Vita port inspired by osu!mania. This is still very much an alpha, but the core game is playable.

Setup

  1. Install the VPK with VitaShell.
  2. Put beatmaps in:

ux0:data/vitamania/

You can drop .osz files directly into that folder. On launch, VitaMania will extract them into:

ux0:data/vitamania/Songs/

If you added new .osz files, the first scan may take a little while.

What Works

vitaMania! can load and play osu! beatmaps on device. 4K mania maps work directly, and standard osu! maps or other key counts are converted to 4K automatically.

Current features include:

  • Playable 4-lane mania gameplay
  • .osz import and auto-extraction
  • Beatmap/song select menu
  • Multiple difficulties grouped under one song
  • MP3 and OGG audio support
  • Background image support
  • Score saving and high scores
  • Pause menu
  • Custom lane binds
  • Basic osu!-style UI and gameplay skinning

Alpha build, so expect bugs and rough edges.

Still To Come

Planned improvements include:

  • Video playback for maps that include videos
  • Custom theme/skin support
  • Optional hit sounds
  • Faster loading and scanning
  • Sorting/filtering in song select
  • More gameplay polish
  • Better results screen
  • More accurate conversion behavior for non-4K maps
  • General bug fixes and performance improvements

Notes

This is an unofficial fan project. Beatmaps can be found here.

PSVitaAlive v.0.8.7

The Case of the Golden Idol - PS Vita Port (v0.8.7)

Originally I just wanted to get trophies working, but I ended up sneaking in a bunch of fixes and QoL updates along the way.

What's New in v0.8.7:

Controls & Input:

  • Cancel button fix: it was mapped to both accept and cancel, so menus closed and immediately reopened. It now only cancels. (issue #4)
  • Volume sync fix: corrected volume synchronization in the project. (issue #3)
  • Help screen: now lists the real PS Vita controls instead of the PC ones (I'll improve it even further in a future version).

Zoom:

  • Progressive zoom: holding L/R or D-Pad Up/Down now zooms smoothly (continuous) instead of fixed steps, for both the scene camera and the Thinking Panel.
  • Thinking Panel zoom (up to 3x): zoom the deduction board to read the text on the small screen.
  • Hint zoom: the hint illustrations can be zoomed and panned the same way.

Visual and UI:

  • Brightness setting: new Settings slider that fades the screen dark or light.
  • Scene-only transitions: the black fade between locations now only covers the scene, keeping the toolbar visible.
  • Overhauled Credits & Discord supporters screens: rolling credits that finish and return automatically.
  • Object-description box: fixed the text centering inside the item description box.

Audio and Video:

  • Intermission videos: re-encoded to a lighter resolution for smoother playback, with the scenario selector hidden behind the video to reduce GPU load.

Performance:

  • DLC crash fix: resolved the C2-12828-1 out-of-memory crash on the Mystery of Monkey Paw Island DLC scene. (issue #2)
  • Project cleanup: unused scenes and prototype images removed from the build (smaller PCK).
  • Extended memory mode: the VPK runs in expanded RAM mode for fewer graphical glitches and smoother gameplay.
    • I tested a low-memory version (the one used for native games). The problem is that limiting the RAM significantly increases load times between scenes and causes a bunch of graphical bugs. I ended up scrapping the idea because the trade-off just isn't worth it. The only real benefit would be the ability to use the browser or listen to music in the background while playing.

Trophies (work in progress)

  • Groundwork for trophy support: TROPHY.TRP generated, Steam -> Vita trophy extraction and .TRP build tools created, and a dedicated plugin under test. Full functionality is not guaranteed yet in this version.

Instructions

Please read the Installation section in the README to learn how to use the patcher tool and install the game on your PS Vita.

⚠️ Note: You MUST legally own the game on Steam to generate the Vita playable files.
